newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bouygues, TF1 heads quizzed in fraud probe.
newsitem.headline: Bouygues, TF1 heads quizzed in fraud probe.

text.p: French police held the chairman of building giant Bouygues in custody on Thursday but released the head of private television channel TF1 overnight after questioning in a fraud probe, justice sources said.

The sources said Martin Bouygues and Philippe Chalendon, managing director of a Bouygues subsidiary, were both being held by police in Versailles after they were summoned on Wednesday for questioning in the probe into false invoices involving some 40 companies in the Paris area.
TF1 head Patrick Le Lay was released at midnight (2300 GMT) on Wednesday. There was no immediate comment from the Bouygues company or from TF1.

The justice sources said Chalendon, managing director of the maritime branch of Bouygues Offshore, would likely be brought before judge Jean-Marie Charpier, who is in charge of the probe launched in 1994, later in the day.
The custody order for Bouygues runs out at 2.30 p.m. (1330 GMT) and a spokesman for the public prosecutor said Bouygues may also be brought before the judge.

The probe focuses on some five million francs ($880,000) worth of allegedly false invoices made out by Cerail consultant firm for subsidiaries of Bouygues including Saur, TF1, Bouygues Offshore and Bouygues Diversifications.
Three managers of the group have already been placed under investigation by the judge.
